summary: Source review identifies a discrepancy with SessionRuntime.update's public promise that every refusal preserves accepted state. AdvanceElapsed first builds next with AccumulatorMicroseconds = total % step, then passes next into advance; when contract.Advance returns Error, advance refuses that already changed state. For a valid running state with step 10000, MaxCatchUpSteps at least 2, old accumulator 0 and elapsed 25000, an advance failure returns accumulator 5000 rather than 0. Product state remains unchanged, but clock state does not. Existing cited tests cover successful elapsed/clamp behavior and input refusal; they do not exercise this failed AdvanceElapsed callback. This is a source-derived counterexample, not an executed CLR reproduction. The owner should resolve whether rollback or the public refusal contract is intended and add the matching adversarial control.
title: Elapsed-time contract failure can change the session accumulator
